reasoning_traces.think:
The triage framework \( \mathcal{L} \) encodes a strategic lattice over four buckets: A (steal), B (research), C (scan), D (hold). Each bucket defines a policy vector \( \vec{\mathcal{P}} \) that maps to GSE’s operational domain. The \( \mathcal{L}_{\text{D}} \) bucket enforces \( \mathcal{F}_{\text{hold}} \), which excludes execution logic and arb bots—this is a dual constraint to \( \mathcal{L}_{\text{A}} \) which allows code/UX reuse. The \( \mathcal{L}_{\text{B}} \) bucket enables offline studies, while \( \mathcal{L}_{\text{C}} \) supports passive observation. The \( \mathcal{F}_{\text{calib}} \) primitive ensures that even in \( \mathcal{L}_{\text{A}} \), only calibrated signals are propagated. The failure mode occurs when \( \mathcal{F}_{\text{hold}} \) is violated by embedding execution logic, leading to misalignment with GSE’s non-execution stance. The \( \mathcal{L}_{\text{D}} \) holds all execution bots and copy-trade tools, which are excluded from any GSE product development. The \( \mathcal{F}_{\text{calib}} \) ensures that even when signals are derived from external models, they are filtered through a confidence threshold \( \alpha \). This prevents overfitting and maintains the integrity of the free spine. The \( \mathcal{L}_{\text{A}} \) bucket allows for borrowing UX and architecture but not execution logic, maintaining a dualistic separation between interface and engine.
